questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment. If no substitution is required select 'No substitution'

__If I would have a degree __from the university, I would get a good job.

options.text: If I am having the degree
When I will have a degree

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **If I had a degree**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "If I had a degree" is an example of a **conditional statement **in the **past tense**. It expresses a hypothetical situation or a condition that is contrary to reality. In this case, the speaker is saying that if they had a degree, they believe that they would have a better chance of getting a good job. However, since the speaker does not currently have a degree, it implies that they do not currently have a good job or may have limited job opportunities.
 
• This type of conditional statement is known as a **second conditional** or **Type 2 conditional**, which is used to talk about hypothetical or unlikely situations in the present or future.
 
• The incident that happens first or was supposed to happen first takes a **past tense (V2 form of verb)** in the ‘If’ clause when **‘would/could/should + V1’** is present in the **main clause** (result).
 
 
• For example: If I had a bike, I would reach on time.
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context,** 'had'** (V2) should be in the 'If' clause because **'would + V1' **(would get) is in the main clause.
 
• Hence, 'If I had a degree' is the correct set of words that must substitute the underlined segment.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct antonym of "**perturb**" is "**soothe**".
 
• The word "**perturb**" means **to cause anxiety or disturbance in someone's mind.**
 
• For example, loud noise or unexpected events can perturb a person. Therefore, the opposite of "**perturb**" would be** to calm or ease someone's mind**, which is the meaning of "**soothe**".
 
• Example sentences using "**perturb**" and "**soothe**":
 
 
• The news of the impending storm was enough to **perturb **even the most seasoned sailors.
 
• The loud music from the party next door **perturbed **her concentration and made it difficult to study.
 
• The gentle sound of the waves and the warm breeze helped **soothe **her troubled mind.
 
 
 
• Hence, **option 2 **is the most appropriate antonym of the word '**Perturb**'.
